title: India's Women Climb to World No. 4, Their Highest-Ever FIH Ranking
excerpt: A 4-0 win over Japan in Bhopal, a day after a 6-2 win over China lifted India to No. 5, took Salima Tete's team to a ranking no Indian women's side has held since the FIH rankings began in 2003.
body:
• India beat Japan 4-0 in Bhopal on November 25 to climb to World No. 4 in the FIH rankings, the highest position in the team's history.
  • The record fell twice in 24 hours: a 6-2 win over China a day earlier had lifted India into the world's top five for the first time.
  • Deepika scored twice against Japan, with Lalremsiami and Neha adding one each, as India finished the Asian Champions Trophy league stage with five wins from five matches and 15 points.
  • India, the defending champions, now face Malaysia in the semi-finals in Bhopal.

India's women's hockey team is ranked fourth in the world, higher than at any point since the FIH World Rankings were introduced in October 2003. A 4-0 win over Japan at the International Sports Complex in Nathu Barkheda, Bhopal, on Wednesday, November 25 completed the climb — one day after a 6-2 win over China had taken India to World No. 5, itself a first.

How the Japan match was won

India's final league match at the Madhya Pradesh Women's Asian Champions Trophy was goalless for 11 minutes before Lalremsiami finished a move kept alive by Navneet Kaur with a reverse flick in the 12th minute, according to Hindusthan Samachar's match report. Deepika converted a penalty corner in the 16th minute to double the lead, and Neha scored from a rebound in the 28th minute after Deepika's initial penalty-corner attempt was saved. Deepika completed her brace in the 48th minute with a penalty-corner strike into the top of the goal. Japan, coached by Akira Takahashi, pressed after half-time but could not break through India's defence.

The win was India's fifth in five league matches, after earlier victories over Malaysia, Thailand, South Korea and China, and it took the defending champions to 15 points at the top of the standings.

Two records in 24 hours

The rise has been steep by the team's own historical standards. According to Hockey India, India's previous best rankings were World No. 9 in 2018, following a quarter-final appearance at the World Cup; World No. 8 after a fourth-place finish at the Tokyo 2020 Olympic Games; and World No. 6 in May–June 2022 after an FIH Pro League campaign, a position the team reached again in 2023. The 6-2 win over China on Tuesday was India's biggest victory over China in the history of the Women's Asian Champions Trophy since a 4-2 win in the 2013 edition.

"Reaching World No. 4 is a proud moment for Indian hockey and a testament to the hard work, discipline and determination of our players and support staff. Achieving this milestone within 24 hours of reaching World No. 5 makes it even more special."

— Bhola Nath Singh, Secretary General, Hockey India

A landmark year

The ranking caps a 2026 season in which, per Hockey India, the team won the FIH Nations Cup, secured a fifth-place finish at the FIH Hockey World Cup — its best since 1974 — and won the Asian Games gold medal after a gap of 44 years. The side is led by captain Salima Tete and coached by Sjoerd Marijne.

What happens next

India face Malaysia in the semi-finals in Bhopal, with both teams unbeaten in the tournament. China play Japan in the second semi-final on November 27. India are chasing a fourth Women's Asian Champions Trophy title and a third consecutive crown.
